doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: State of jazz today and the tunes on Willcox's CDs
summary: Gallodoro thinks jazz is coming back with college kids; Willcox discusses standards he recorded, including That's My Home, Poor Butterfly and Danny Barker's Ham and Eggs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I’m looking forward to hearing these, both of your recordings, guys, and what do you think of the state of jazz today?

I think it’s coming back. I really think if more college kids begin to hear more of it they like it. I know that they like it. Because we have chord changes, we have melody. There’s something there. And it isn’t monotonous. It isn’t one thing after another.
Well you brought up tunes, well you can almost tell from all of them, they’re all, most of them are what we call old standards. There a tune there called “That’s My Home,” is that one on that?
Way back when I was 89. That’s my other tune that I heard, that’s the theme song—
Oh, I think Doc Cheatham recorded this recently. “That’s My Home,” yes.
Did he really? Well it’s a pretty tune. Yes it is. Yeah and then another tune on there is “Poor Butterfly,” that’s been my theme song—
That’s been my theme song for 65 years.

Pretty, pretty, pretty. Yeah and now and the other, oh this is interesting, this last one I made was that was last summer, with practically the same band, all in Holland, Dutch musicians. The first one is called “Ham and Eggs,” and last year I was playing at Tivoli Gardens in Copenhagen. That’s a big park. If you ever go to Copenhagen, you’re bound to go to Tivoli Gardens. And I was playing the JazzHouse with the number one jazz band of Denmark. And this “Ham and Eggs” was a tune that they were playing, and I sing © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

now, and I said I’m going to take that with me right in my head, because I knew I was going to record in Holland the next week, and it was written by, what I’m leading up to, it was written by Danny Barker, the guitar player, you know the black guy, he just died here two or three years ago. And well anyway, it’s not real fast and not too slow. But just a nice, cute song.
